questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the Maclaurin series expansion e^x = 1 + x + x^2/2! + x^3/3! + ...; the numerator simplifies to x^3/6 + higher order terms, so the limit is 1/6. Full Solution: Apply L'Hospital's Rule three times: lim (e^x - 1 - x)/3x^2 = lim (e^x - 1)/6x = lim e^x/6 = 1/6.

questions.text: A block of mass 2 kg rests on a rough horizontal surface. A horizontal force of 10 N is applied. The coefficient of static friction μs is 0.3. Using the quick check that maximum static friction = μs·mg, will the block move?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because applied force > maximum static friction

options.label: B
options.text: No, because applied force < maximum static friction

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, because kinetic friction is lower

options.label: D
options.text: No, because the surface is frictionless

questions.solution: Shortcut: Compute max static friction = μs·mg = 0.3·2·10 = 6 N. Since applied 10 N > 6 N, block will start moving. Full steps: f_max = μs N = μs mg = 0.3×2×9.8 ≈ 5.88 N (≈6 N). 10 N > 5.88 N, so motion occurs. Hence option A is correct.

questions.text: According to the ideal gas law, at constant volume, pressure is directly proportional to temperature (in Kelvin). If a sealed container initially at 300 Khas pressure 1.0 atm, what is the pressure when the temperature is raised to 450 K? Use the shortcut ratio P2/P1 = T2/T1.
questions.solution: Shortcut: P2 = P1·(T2/T1) = 1.0·(450/300) = 1·1.5 = 1.5 atm. Full steps: Convert temperatures to Kelvin (already given). Ratio = 450/300 = 1.5. Multiply by initial pressure 1.0 atm gives 1.5 atm. Option A is correct.

questions.text: A uniform disc of mass Mand radius R has a concentric circular hole of radius R/2 cut out from it. The moment of inertia of the remaining part about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through its centre is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: The removed disc has mass M/4 (area ratio) and MI = 1/2*(M/4)*(R/2)^2 = MR^2/32. Full disc MI = 1/2 MR^2 = 16/32 MR^2. Subtracting gives 15/32 MR^2. Full solution: MI of full disc = ½MR². Mass of hole = M*(π(R/2)²)/(πR²) = M/4. MI of hole about same axis = ½*(M/4)*(R/2)² = MR²/32. MI remaining = ½MR² - MR²/32 = (16/32 - 1/32)MR² = 15/32 MR².

questions.text: One mole of a monoatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) expands adiabatically from volume V to 2V. If the initial temperature is T0, the final temperature is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For adiabatic process TV^(γ-1)=constant. Here γ-1 = 2/3, so T_f = T0 (V_i/V_f)^(2/3) = T0/2^(2/3). Full solution: Adiabatic relation T V^(γ-1) = constant. With γ = 5/3, γ-1 = 2/3. Initial state: T0 V^(2/3). Final state: T_f (2V)^(2/3). Equating gives T_f = T0 (V/(2V))^(2/3) = T0/2^(2/3).

questions.text: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle of mass m moving with kinetic energy K is λ. If the kinetic energy is increased to 4K, the new wavelength becomes:
questions.solution: Shortcut: λ = h/√(2mK) ∝ 1/√K. Quadrupling K makes λ half. Full solution: de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p, with p = √(2mK). So λ = h/√(2mK). If K → 4K, new λ' = h/√(2m·4K) = h/(2√(2mK)) = λ/2.

questions.text: For a first-order reaction, the half-life is 20 minutes. The time required for 75% completion of the reaction is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: 75% completion corresponds to two half-lives (50% in first, 25% in second). Time = 2 × t₁/₂ = 2 × 20 = 40 min. Full Solution: For a first-order reaction, t₁/₂ = 0.693/k. Fraction remaining after time t is (1/2)^(t/t₁/₂). For 75% completion, fraction remaining = 0.25 = (1/2)², so t/t₁/₂ = 2 → t = 40 min.

questions.text: Which of the following carbocations is most stabilized by hyperconjugation?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Hyperconjugation stability ∝ number of α-hydrogens. CH₃⁺ (0 α-H), CH₃CH₂⁺ (3 α-H), (CH₃)₂CH⁺ (6 α-H), (CH₃)₃C⁺ (9 α-H). Maximum α-H gives maximum stability. Full Solution: Hyperconjugation involves delocalization of σ-electrons of C-H bonds (α to the positive charge) into the empty p-orbital. The tert-butyl cation (CH₃)₃C⁺ has 9 α-hydrogens, the highest among the options, leading to the greatest charge dispersal and stability.

questions.text: The correct decreasing order of acidic strength for the oxoacids of chlorine is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Acidic strength of oxoacids increases with the oxidation state of the central atom (or number of terminal oxygen atoms). Oxidation states: HClO (+1), HClO₂ (+3), HClO₃ (+5), HClO₄ (+7). Order: HClO₄ > HClO₃ > HClO₂ > HClO. Full Solution: Higher oxidation state increases electron withdrawal from the O-H bond, facilitating proton release. The conjugate base stability also increases with more terminal oxygens (greater resonance delocalization of negative charge). Thus, perchloric acid (HClO₄) is the strongest.

questions.text: The standard electrode potentials are: Zn²⁺/Zn = –0.76 V, Cu²⁺/Cu = +0.34 V. For the cell Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(0.1 M) || Cu²⁺(0.01 M) | Cu(s) at 298 K, the EMF of the cell is approximately:
questions.solution: Shortcut: E°cell = 0.34 – (–0.76) = 1.10 V. Since the reaction quotient Q = [Zn²⁺]/[Cu²⁺] = 10, the Nernst term at 298 K is (0.0591/2)log10 = 0.02955 V. Subtracting gives 1.10 – 0.02955 ≈ 1.07 V. Stepwise: E°cell = 1.10 V; n = 2; E = E° – (0.0591/n) log Q = 1.10 – 0.02955 × 1 = 1.07045 V ≈ 1.07 V.

questions.text: The decreasing order of reactivity towards SN2 reaction for the following alkyl bromides is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: SN2 reactivity decreases with increasing steric hindrance: methyl > primary > secondary > tertiary. Option A follows this order exactly. Stepwise: CH₃Br (methyl) least hindered, fastest; CH₃CH₂Br (primary) next; (CH₃)₂CHBr (secondary) slower; (CH₃)₃CBr (tertiary) essentially no SN2. Hence the correct sequence is CH₃Br > CH₃CH₂Br > (CH₃)₂CHBr > (CH₃)₃CBr.

questions.text: The value of the definite integral ∫₀^π (x sin x) / (1 + cos² x) dx is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply King's Property I = ∫₀^π f(x)dx = ∫₀^π f(π-x)dx. Adding, 2I = π ∫₀^π sin x/(1+cos² x) dx. Substitute t = cos x ⇒ dt = -sin x dx. Integral = π [tan⁻¹(cos x)]_π⁰ = π(π/4 + π/4) = π²/2 ⇒ I = π²/4. Step-by-step: Let I be the integral. Replace x by π-x, add the two equations to remove x from numerator. Evaluate resulting integral using substitution cos x = t.

questions.text: Two fair dice are rolled simultaneously. The probability that the sum of the numbers appearing is a prime number is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Total outcomes = 36. Prime sums possible: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11. Favourable pairs: Sum 2 (1), Sum 3 (2), Sum 5 (4), Sum 7 (6), Sum 11 (2). Total favourable = 15. Probability = 15/36 = 5/12. Step-by-step: List all 36 ordered pairs. Identify pairs giving prime sums (2,3,5,7,11). Count frequency: (1,1); (1,2),(2,1); (1,4),(2,3),(3,2),(4,1); (1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1); (5,6),(6,5). Divide 15 by 36.

questions.text: The area of the triangle formed by the lines x = 0, y = 0 and 3x + 4y = 12 is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: The line 3x+4y=12 cuts axes at (4,0) and (0,3). With coordinate axes, it forms a right triangle. Area = ½ × x-intercept × y-intercept = ½ × 4 × 3 = 6 sq units. Step-by-step: Find x-intercept by setting y=0 ⇒ 3x=12 ⇒ x=4. Find y-intercept by setting x=0 ⇒ 4y=12 ⇒ y=3. Vertices are (0,0), (4,0), (0,3). Use right triangle area formula ½ × base × height.

questions.text: If z = (1 + i)^6, then the value of |z| is:
The coefficient of x^2 in the expansion of (1 + x)^7 is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: The coefficient of x^r in (1+x)^n is nCr; here n=7, r=2 gives 7C2 = 21. Full: Expand using binomial theorem: (1+x)^7 = Σ_{k=0}^7 7Ck x^k; the term with x^2 is 7C2 x^2 = 21 x^2.

questions.text: A projectile is fired with an initial speed u at an angle θ with the horizontal. Its range is R. For the same initial speed u, there is another angle of projection that yields the same range R. If the ratio of the maximum heights attained in the two cases is 1 : 4, the value of tan θ is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For complementary angles θ and (90°−θ) giving the same range, the ratio of maximum heights H₁/H₂ = tan²θ. Given H₁/H₂ = 1/4, we get tan²θ = 1/4 ⇒ tan θ = 1/2. Full Solution: Range R = u²sin2θ/g. Same range occurs for θ and 90°−θ. H₁ = u²sin²θ/2g, H₂ = u²cos²θ/2g. Ratio H₁/H₂ = tan²θ = 1/4 ⇒ tan θ = 1/2.

questions.text: A point charge q is placed at one corner of a cube of side a. The electric flux through each of the three faces meeting at that corner is zero. What is the electric flux through each of the remaining three faces of the cube?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Enclose the charge symmetrically by imagining 8 such cubes forming a larger cube with the charge at the centre. Total flux = q/ε₀. Flux through one small cube = q/(8ε₀). The 3 faces touching the charge have zero flux (field lines parallel). The remaining flux q/(8ε₀) is shared equally by the 3 opposite faces. Flux per face = q/(24ε₀). Full Solution: By Gauss's law, total flux from charge q is q/ε₀. Placing the charge at the corner of a cube means it is shared by 8 identical cubes meeting at that corner. Flux entering the given cube = q/(8ε₀). The electric field is radial; hence it is parallel to the three faces meeting at the corner, giving zero flux through them. The entire flux q/(8ε₀) must exit through the three opposite faces. By symmetry, each of these three faces gets one-third: (1/3) × q/(8ε₀) = q/(24ε₀).

questions.text: Two long straight parallel wires separated by a distance d carry currents I and 2I respectively in the same direction. The magnetic force per unit length experienced by the wire carrying current I is F. If the current in the first wire is doubled and the separation between the wires is halved, the new force per unit length on the first wire becomes:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Force per unit length f ∝ (I₁ I₂)/d. Initially f = F ∝ (I × 2I)/d = 2I²/d. New: I₁' = 2I, I₂' = 2I (unchanged), d' = d/2. New force f' ∝ (2I × 2I)/(d/2) = 4I² × (2/d) = 8I²/d. Ratio f'/F = (8I²/d) / (2I²/d) = 4. Answer is 4F. Full Solution: The force per unit length between two parallel currents is given by f = (μ₀/2π) (I₁ I₂/d). Initial force F = (μ₀/2π) (I × 2I)/d = (μ₀/2π) (2I²/d). After changes: I₁ = 2I, I₂ = 2I, d = d/2. New force F' = (μ₀/2π) (2I × 2I)/(d/2) = (μ₀/2π) (4I² × 2/d) = (μ₀/2π) (8I²/d) = 4 × [(μ₀/2π) (2I²/d)] = 4F.

questions.text: In a Young's double slit experiment using light of wavelength λ, the central bright fringe is observed at point O on the screen. A thin transparent sheet of refractive index μ = 1.5 and thickness t is introduced in front of the upper slit. Consequently, the central maximum shifts to a position originally occupied by the 5tho rder bright fringe. The thickness t of the sheet in terms of λ is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Shift of central maximum by n fringes implies path difference introduced = nλ. Path difference by sheet = (μ - 1)t. Equate: (μ - 1)t = nλ. Here n=5, μ=1.5. (0.5)t = 5λ ⇒ t = 10λ. Full Solution: Introduction of a sheet of thickness t and refractive index μ in front of a slit increases the optical path by (μ - 1)t. For the central maximum to shift to the position of the 5th bright fringe, the path difference must equal 5λ. Thus, (μ - 1)t = 5λ. Substituting μ = 1.5 gives (1.5 - 1)t = 5λ ⇒ 0.5t = 5λ ⇒ t = 10λ.

questions.text: A metallic rod of length L rotates with a constant angular velocity ω in a uniform magnetic field B perpendicular to the plane of rotation, about an axis passing through one end. The emf induced between the ends of the rod is ε. The rod is replaced by another rod of length 2L made of the same material, rotating at angular velocity ω/2 in the same magnetic field. The new induced emf is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Motional emf in a rotating rod ε = (1/2) B ω L². ε ∝ ω L². New ω' = ω/2 (factor 1/2). New L' = 2L (factor 4). Net factor = (1/2) × 4 = 2. New emf = 2ε. Full Solution: For a rod rotating about one end in a perpendicular magnetic field, the emf induced between the ends is derived by integrating the motional emf of elements: ε = ∫₀ᴸ B ω r dr = (1/2) B ω L². For the new rod, L' = 2Land ω' = ω/2. New emf ε' = (1/2) B (ω/2) (2L)² = (1/2) B (ω/2) (4L²) = (1/2) B ω L² × 2 = 2ε.
questions.topic: EMI - Motional EMF in Rotating Rod

questions.text: The solubility product (Ksp) of AgCl is 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ at 298 K. What is the molar solubility of AgCl in a 0.1 M NaCl solution? (Assume volume change is negligible)
questions.solution: Shortcut: In presence of a common ion (Cl⁻ from NaCl), solubility S ≈ Ksp / [Common Ion] = 1.8×10⁻¹⁰ / 0.1 = 1.8×10⁻⁹ M. Full Solution: Let S be solubility. [Ag⁺] = S, [Cl⁻] = 0.1 + S ≈ 0.1. Ksp = [Ag⁺][Cl⁻] = S × 0.1 = 1.8×10⁻¹⁰ ⇒ S = 1.8×10⁻⁹ M.
questions.topic: Ionic Equilibrium - Solubility Product & Common Ion Effect

questions.text: An element with atomic mass 108 g mol⁻¹ crystallizes in an FCC lattice. If the density of the crystal is 10.5 g cm⁻³, what is the edge length of the unit cell? (Nₐ = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
questions.solution: Shortcut: For FCC, Z=4. Use ρ = (Z×M)/(Nₐ×a³) ⇒ a³ = (4×108)/(10.5×6.022×10²³) = 6.83×10⁻²³ cm³ ⇒ a = 4.09×10⁻⁸ cm = 409 pm. Full Solution: Rearrange density formula for a³. Substitute Z=4 (FCC), M=108, ρ=10.5, Nₐ=6.022×10²³. Calculate a³ = 6.83×10⁻²³ cm³. Cube root gives a ≈ 4.09×10⁻⁸ cm = 409 pm.
questions.topic: Solid State - Density & Unit Cell Parameters

questions.text: Butanamide (CH₃CH₂CH₂CONH₂) is treated with Br₂ and NaOH (Hofmann Bromamide reaction). The major organic product formed is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Hofmann rearrangement degrades amide to amine with ONE LESS carbon (loss of carbonyl carbon as CO₂). Butanamide (C4) → Propanamine (C3). Full Solution: R-CONH₂ + Br₂ + 4NaOH → R-NH₂ + Na₂CO₃ + 2NaBr + 2H₂O. The alkyl group R migrates to nitrogen. For Butanamide, R = CH₃CH₂CH₂⁻ (propyl). Product is CH₃CH₂CH₂NH₂ (Propanamine).
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Named Reactions (Hofmann Bromamide Degradation)

questions.text: The half-life of a reaction is found to be 10 minutes when the initial concentration of the reactant is 0.1 M. When the initial concentration is reduced to 0.05 M, the half-life becomes 20 minutes. The order of the reaction is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For any order n, t₁/₂ ∝ 1/[A]₀ⁿ⁻¹. Here concentration halved (ratio 1/2) and t₁/₂ doubled (ratio 2). So 2 = (1/2)ⁿ⁻¹ ⇒ 2 = 2¹⁻ⁿ ⇒ 1 = 1−n ⇒ n=2. Full Solution: Using the half-life dependence on initial concentration, t₁/₂ = k' / [A]₀ⁿ⁻¹. Taking ratio: t₁/₂(2)/t₁/₂(1) = ([A]₀(1)/[A]₀(2))ⁿ⁻¹. Substituting 20/10 = (0.1/0.05)ⁿ⁻¹ gives 2 = 2ⁿ⁻¹, hence n−1 = 1 and n = 2.

questions.text: The quantity of electricity (in Coulombs) required to deposit 27 g of aluminium (Atomic mass = 27 g mol⁻¹) from an aqueous solution of Al³⁺ ions is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Equivalents = Mass / Equivalent Weight. Eq. wt of Al = 27/3 = 9. Equivalents = 27/9 = 3. Charge = Equivalents × F = 3 × 96500 = 289500 C. Full Solution: The reduction half-reaction is Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al. 3 moles of electrons (3F) are required to deposit 1 mole (27 g) of Al. Using Faraday'sse cond law, Q = (mass × n × F) / M = (27 × 3 × 96500) / 27 = 3 × 96500 = 289500 C.

questions.text: If \(\displaystyle \lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\sin 5x}{\tan 3x}=k\), then \(k\) equals:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Near zero, \(\sin θ≈θ\) and \(\tan θ≈θ\). So \(\frac{\sin 5x}{\tan 3x}\approx\frac{5x}{3x}=\frac{5}{3}\). Full solution: Using the standard limits \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin ax}{ax}=1\) and \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\tan bx}{bx}=1\), rewrite the expression as \(\frac{5x}{3x}\cdot\frac{\sin 5x}{5x}\cdot\frac{3x}{\tan 3x}\). Both fractions tend to 1, leaving \(\frac{5}{3}\).

questions.text: Evaluate the determinant \[\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & k \\ 3 & k & 9 \end{vmatrix}=0\] Find the value of \(k\).
questions.solution: Shortcut: Notice rows are proportional when k=6 because second row =2×first row except last entry: 2×3=6, so set k=6 makes determinant zero instantly. Full solution: Expand determinant or use row operations: R2→R2-2R1 gives (0,0,k-6). R3→R3-3R1 gives (0,k-6,0). Determinant = (k-6)·(k-6)·1 = (k-6)^2. Setting to zero gives k=6.

questions.text: Evaluate the definite integral \( \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin^3 x}{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x} \, dx \).
questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply King's Property \( I = \int_a^b f(x) dx = \int_a^b f(a+b-x) dx \). Replacing \( x \) by \( \pi/2 - x \) converts the integrand to \( \cos^3 x/(\cos^3 x + \sin^3 x) \). Adding the original and transformed integrals gives \( 2I = \int_0^{\pi/2} 1 \, dx = \pi/2 \), so \( I = \pi/4 \). Full: Let \( I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin^3 x}{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x} dx \). Using \( x \to \pi/2 - x \), \( I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{\cos^3 x}{\cos^3 x + \sin^3 x} dx \). Adding: \( 2I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x}{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x} dx = \int_0^{\pi/2} dx = \frac{\pi}{2} \). Thus \( I = \frac{\pi}{4} \).

questions.text: Tangents are drawn from a variable point P on the line \( x + y = 4 \) to the parabola \( y^2 = 8x \). The chord of contact of these tangents always passes through a fixed point. The coordinates of this fixed point are:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Chord of contact from \( (h,k) \) to \( y^2=4ax \) is \( ky = 2a(x+h) \). Here \( a=2 \), so \( ky = 4(x+h) \). Since \( P(h,k) \) lies on \( x+y=4 \), \( h = 4-k \). Substitute: \( ky = 4(x+4-k) \Rightarrow 4x - ky + 16 - 4k = 0 \Rightarrow 4(x+4) = k(y+4) \). This family of lines passes through the intersection of \( x+4=0 \) and \( y+4=0 \), i.e., \( (-4, -4) \). Full: For \( y^2=8x \), \( a=2 \). Chord of contact from \( (x_1, y_1) \) is \( yy_1 = 4(x+x_1) \). Let \( P \equiv (h, k) \) on \( x+y=4 \Rightarrow h=4-k \). Chord: \( ky = 4(x+4-k) \Rightarrow 4x - ky + 16 - 4k = 0 \Rightarrow 4(x+4) - k(y+4) = 0 \). This represents a line passing through the fixed point \( (-4, -4) \) for all \( k \).

questions.text: A fair coin is tossed 5 times. Given that at least 3 heads have appeared, the probability that exactly 4 heads appear is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use conditional probability \( P(A|B) = P(A)/P(B) \) since \( A \subset B \). \( P(\text{exactly 4 heads}) = {}^5C_4/2^5 = 5/32 \). \( P(\text{at least 3 heads}) = (^{5}C_3 + ^{5}C_4 + ^{5}C_5)/2^5 = 16/32 = 1/2 \). Required probability \( = (5/32) \div (1/2) = 5/16 \). Full: Total outcomes \( = 2^5 = 32 \). Event A (exactly 4 heads): \( n(A) = {}^5C_4 = 5 \). Event B (at least 3 heads): \( n(B) = {}^5C_3 + {}^5C_4 + {}^5C_5 = 10 + 5 + 1 = 16 \). Since \( A \subset B \), \( P(A|B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)} = \frac{P(A)}{P(B)} = \frac{5/32}{16/32} = \frac{5}{16} \).

questions.text: Two identical balls A and Bare moving along the same straight line with velocities +v and -2v respectively. They undergo a perfectly elastic head-on collision. The velocities of A and B after the collision are:
questions.solution: Shortcut: In a 1D elastic collision between equal masses, velocities are exchanged. Worked: Let u₁ = +v, u₂ = -2v. Conservation of momentum: v₁ + v₂ = -v. Coefficient of restitution e=1: v₂ - v₁ = u₁ - u₂ = 3v. Solving gives v₁ = -2v, v₂ = +v.

questions.text: Two thin lenses of focal lengths +20 cm and -30 cm are placed in contact. The equivalent focal length of the combination is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use power addition in Dioptres. P = P1 + P2 = (100/20) + (100/-30) = 5 - 3.33 = +1.67 D. Equivalent focal length f = 100/P = 100/1.67 ≈ +60 cm. Full Solution: For thin lenses in contact, 1/F = 1/f1 + 1/f2. Substituting f1 = +20 cm, f2 = -30 cm: 1/F = 1/20 - 1/30 = (3-2)/60 = 1/60. Thus F = +60 cm. The positive sign indicates a converging combination.

questions.text: In a potentiometer experiment, a cell of emf 1.5 V gives a balancing length of 60 cm. If this cell is replaced by another cell of emf 2.0 V, the new balancing length (in cm) will be:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Balancing length L is directly proportional to emf E (L ∝ E) for a constant potential gradient. L2 = L1 × (E2/E1) = 60 × (2.0/1.5) = 60 × (4/3) = 80 cm. Full Solution: Potential gradient k = E1/L1 = 1.5/60 = 0.025 V/cm. For the second cell, E2 = k × L2 ⇒ L2 = E2/k = 2.0 / 0.025 = 80 cm.

questions.text: In a photoelectric effect experiment, the stopping potential V_s is plotted against the frequency f of incident light. The slope of the straight line obtained gives:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Einstein's equation eV_s = hf - φ ⇒ V_s = (h/e)f - φ/e. This is a straight line y = mx + c where slope m = h/e. Full Solution: The graph of stopping potential vs frequency is linear. Comparing V_s = (h/e)f - φ/e with y = mx + c, the slope is h/e. The intercept on the frequency axis gives threshold frequency f0 = φ/h, and the intercept on the V_s axis gives -φ/e.

questions.text: Two long coaxial solenoids of same length l and cross-sectional area A have N1 and N2 turns respectively. The mutual inductance M between them is proportional to:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Mutual inductance M = μ0 N1 N2 A / l for long coaxial solenoids. Thus M ∝ N1 N2 A / l. Option elimination: M must depend on geometry (A, l) and product of turns (N1 N2), not sum. Full Solution: Magnetic field due to inner solenoid B = μ0 n1 I1 = μ0 (N1/l) I1. Flux through each turn of outer solenoid Φ = B A = μ0 (N1/l) I1 A. Total flux linkage with outer solenoid = N2 Φ = μ0 N1 N2 A I1 / l. By definition M = (Flux linkage)/I1 = μ0 N1 N2 A / l.

questions.text: The sum of the infinite series \( 1 + \frac{4}{5} + \frac{7}{5^2} + \frac{10}{5^3} + \dots \) is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Recognize as an Arithmetico-Geometric Progression (AGP) with first term \(a=1\), common difference \(d=3\), and common ratio \(r=1/5\). Use the direct formula \(S_\infty = \frac{a}{1-r} + \frac{dr}{(1-r)^2} = \frac{1}{4/5} + \frac{3(1/5)}{(4/5)^2} = \frac{5}{4} + \frac{15}{16} = \frac{35}{16}\). Full Solution: Let \(S = 1 + \frac{4}{5} + \frac{7}{25} + \frac{10}{125} + \dots\). Multiply by \(r=1/5\): \(\frac{S}{5} = \frac{1}{5} + \frac{4}{25} + \frac{7}{125} + \dots\). Subtract: \(S - \frac{S}{5} = 1 + \frac{3}{5} + \frac{3}{25} + \frac{3}{125} + \dots = 1 + \frac{3/5}{1-1/5} = 1 + \frac{3}{4} = \frac{7}{4}\). Thus \(\frac{4S}{5} = \frac{7}{4} \Rightarrow S = \frac{35}{16}\).

questions.text: What is the unit digit of 7^{2023}?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The unit digits of powers of 7 repeat every 4: 7, 9, 3, 1. Since 2023 mod 4 = 3, the unit digit is the third in the cycle, which is 3. Full solution: 7^1=7, 7^2=49→9, 7^3=343→3, 7^4=2401→1. The cycle length is 4. 2023 = 4×505 + 3, so 7^{2023} has the same unit digit as 7^3 = 3.

questions.text: Find the remainder when 2^{100} is divided by 7.
questions.solution: Shortcut: By Fermat's little theorem, 2^6 ≡ 1 (mod 7). 100 = 6×16 + 4, so 2^{100} ≡ (2^6)^{16}·2^4 ≡ 1^{16}·16 ≡ 2 (mod 7). Full solution: Compute powers of 2 modulo 7: 2^1=2, 2^2=4, 2^3=8≡1, 2^4=2, 2^5=4, 2^6=1. The cycle length is 3. 100 mod 3 = 1, so 2^{100} ≡ 2^1 = 2 mod 7. Both methods give remainder 2.

questions.text: Using the first two terms of the binomial expansion, the approximate value of (1.01)^5 is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For small x, (1+x)^n ≈ 1 + nx. Here x=0.01, n=5, so approximation = 1 + 5×0.01 = 1.05. Full solution: Binomial expansion (1+x)^5 = 1 + 5x + 10x^2 + 10x^3 + 5x^4 + x^5. With x=0.01, the first two terms give 1 + 0.05 = 1.05. The next term 10x^2 = 10×0.0001 = 0.001, so actual value ≈ 1.051. The question asks for the approximation using only the first two terms, which is 1.05.

questions.text: The number of distinct real roots of the cubic equation x^3 - 3x + 1 = 0 is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use calculus. f(x)=x^3-3x+1, f'(x)=3x^2-3=3(x-1)(x+1). Critical points at x=±1. f(-1)=3>0, f(1)=-1<0. Since the cubic goes from -∞ to +∞ and has a local maximum positive and local minimum negative, it crosses the x-axis three times. Hence three distinct real roots. Full solution: The discriminant Δ = -4(-3)^3 - 27(1)^2 = 108 - 27 = 81 > 0, confirming three distinct real roots.

questions.text: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 150 V. The de Broglie wavelength associated with the electron is approximately: (Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C)
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the direct formula λ(Å) = 12.27/√V. For V = 150 V, λ = 12.27/√150 ≈ 12.27/12.25 ≈ 1.00 Å. Full Solution: Kinetic energy E = eV = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ × 150 = 2.4×10⁻¹⁷ J. Momentum p = √(2mE) = √(2 × 9.1×10⁻³¹ × 2.4×10⁻¹⁷) ≈ 6.62×10⁻²⁴ kg m/s. λ = h/p = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ / 6.62×10⁻²⁴ ≈ 1.00×10⁻¹⁰ m = 1.00 Å.

questions.text: The spin-only magnetic moment (in Bohr Magneton) of the complex ion [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺ is closest to:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Fe²⁺ is d⁶. H₂O is a weak field ligand → high spin configuration (t₂g⁴ eg²) → 4 unpaired electrons. Use μ = √[n(n+2)] = √[4×6] = √24 ≈ 4.90 BM. Full Solution: Electronic configuration of Fe²⁺ is [Ar] 3d⁶. In an octahedral field with weak field ligand H₂O, pairing energy > CFSE, so high spin: t₂g⁴ eg². Number of unpaired electrons n = 4. Spin-only formula μ = √[n(n+2)] BM = √[4(6)] = √24 = 4.899 ≈ 4.90 BM.

questions.text: For a reaction at 298 K, ΔH = +50 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS = +100 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. The minimum temperature (in K) above which the reaction becomes spontaneous is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Spontaneity requires ΔG < 0. At equilibrium ΔG = 0 = ΔH - TΔS → T = ΔH/ΔS. Convert ΔH to J: 50,000 J mol⁻¹. T = 50,000 / 100 = 500 K. Reaction spontaneous for T > 500 K. Full Solution: Gibbs free energy ΔG = ΔH - TΔS. For spontaneity, ΔG < 0 ⇒ ΔH - TΔS < 0 ⇒ T > ΔH/ΔS. Given ΔH = +50 kJ mol⁻¹ = 50,000 J mol⁻¹ and ΔS = +100 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. T = 50,000 J mol⁻¹ / 100 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ = 500 K. Thus, above 500 K the reaction is spontaneous.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds will NOT give a positive iodoform test (yellow precipitate of CHI₃) with I₂/NaOH?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Iodoform test is given by compounds containing CH₃CO– (methyl ketone) or CH₃CH(OH)– (secondary alcohol with methyl adjacent to carbinol carbon) which oxidize to methyl ketones. Ethanol → CH₃CHO (gives test). Acetaldehyde → CH₃CHO (gives test). Acetone → CH₃COCH₃ (gives test). Benzaldehyde (PhCHO) lacks CH₃CO– group → No test. Full Solution: The iodoform reaction requires a CH₃C=O or CH₃CH(OH) group. Ethanol oxidizes to acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO) which has CH₃CO–. Acetaldehyde has CH₃CO–. Acetone is CH₃COCH₃. Benzaldehyde is C₆H₅CHO; the carbonyl carbon is attached to Hand Ph, notch₃. Hence, it does not respond.
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Carbonyl Compounds / Qualitative Analysis

questions.text: Which of the following molecules has a net dipole moment of zero?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Check molecular geometry symmetry. BF₃ is trigonal planar (sp², 120°) with three identical B–F bonds → vector sum = 0. NH₃ (pyramidal), H₂O (bent), SO₂ (bent) are asymmetrical → net μ > 0. Full Solution: Dipole moment is a vector quantity. BF₃ has trigonal planar geometry (D₃h symmetry); the three B–F bond dipoles are at 120° and cancel each other resulting in μ = 0. NH₃ (C₃v, pyramidal), H₂O (C₂v, bent), and SO₂ (C₂v, bent) have resultant dipole moments due to their asymmetric shapes and lone pairs.
questions.topic: Chemical Bonding - Molecular Geometry & Dipole Moment

questions.text: A projectile is launched with an initial speed u at an angle θ with the horizontal and attains a range R. If the launch angle is changed to (90°−θ) while keeping the speed same, the new range will be:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For complementary angles θ and (90°−θ), sin(2θ) = sin(180°−2θ), so the range formula R = u² sin(2θ)/g gives the same range. Full solution: Using R = u² sin(2θ)/g, the new range R' = u² sin(2(90°−θ))/g = u² sin(180°−2θ)/g = u² sin(2θ)/g = R.

questions.text: A mass m attached to a spring of force constant k oscillates with a time period T. The mass is replaced by 4m and the spring constant is changed to k/2. The new time period of oscillation is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Time period T ∝ √(m/k); the ratio T'/T = √((4m)/(k/2) ÷ (m/k)) = √8 = 2√2. Full solution: T = 2π√(m/k); new T' = 2π√(4m/(k/2)) = 2π√(8m/k) = √8 × 2π√(m/k) = 2√2 T.

questions.text: Two identical capacitors each of capacitance Care connected in series. This series combination is then connected in parallel with a third identical capacitor C. The equivalent capacitance of the entire arrangement is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Two capacitors in series give C/2; adding a third in parallel adds C, yielding C/2 + C = 3C/2. Full solution: Series equivalent C_s = (C×C)/(C+C) = C/2. Parallel with C gives C_eq = C_s + C = C/2 + C = 3C/2.

questions.text: A radioactive sample has a half‑life of T. After a time interval of 3T, the activity of the sample becomes:
questions.solution: Shortcut: After n half‑lives activity reduces by (1/2)ⁿ; for n=3, factor = 1/8. Full solution: Activity A = A₀(1/2)^(t/T); with t=3T, A = A₀(1/2)³ = A₀/8.

questions.text: A Carnot engine has an efficiency of 40%. If the temperature of the cold reservoir is 300 K, the temperature of the hot reservoir is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Efficiency η = 1 − T_c/T_h ⇒ T_h = T_c/(1−η) = 300/(0.6) = 500 K. Full solution: 0.40 = 1 − 300/T_h → 300/T_h = 0.60 → T_h = 300/0.60 = 500 K.

questions.text: As per the table, the percentage yield of a reaction was calculated using the mass of product obtained. Which of the following statements is a correct shortcut to quickly estimate the percentage yield? Table: | Theoretical mass (g) | Actual mass (g) | |----------------------|-----------------| | 45.0 | 36.0 |

options.label: A
options.text: Multiply actual mass by 100 and divide by theoretical mass.

options.label: B
options.text: Subtract actual mass from theoretical mass, then divide by theoretical mass and multiply by 100.

options.label: C
options.text: Add actual and theoretical masses, then divide by 2 and multiply by 100.

options.label: D
options.text: Divide theoretical mass by actual mass and multiply by 100.

questions.solution: Shortcut: % yield = (actual / theoretical) ×100; just a direct ratio, no extra steps. Full solution: % yield = (36.0 g / 45.0 g) ×100 = 0.8×100 = 80 %. Option A states the exact shortcut.

questions.text: The following data represent the absorbance (A) of a solution measured at different concentrations (c, mol L⁻¹). Using Beer's law (A = εlc, l = 1 cm), which concentration gives the highest absorbance? Table: | c (mol L⁻¹) | A | |------------|---| | 0.10 | 0.45 | | 0.25 | 1.12 | | 0.40 | 1.78 | | 0.55 | 2.45 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: In Beer's law absorbance is directly proportional to concentration; the largest concentration gives the largest absorbance. Full solution: Compare the A values – they increase with c. The highest A (2.45) corresponds to c = 0.55 mol L⁻¹. Hence option D (index 3).

questions.text: The following data give the rate of formation of product (mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹) at different concentrations of reactant A (mol L⁻¹). Using the method of initial rates, determine the order of reaction with respect to A. Table: | [A] (mol L⁻¹) | Rate (×10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹) | |---------------|--------------------------| | 0.10 | 2.0 | | 0.20 | 8.0 | | 0.40 | 32.0 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Compare how rate changes when concentration doubles. If rate quadruples, order is 2 (since 2²=4). Full solution: From 0.10→0.20 M, [A] doubles, rate goes from 2.0→8.0 (×4). Doubling again (0.20→0.40 M) gives rate 8.0→32.0 (×4). Consistent factor of 4 for each doubling ⇒ rate ∝ [A]². Hence second order. Option C (index 2).

questions.text: An aqueous solution of a weak binary electrolyte AB (concentration 0.1 mol L⁻¹) exhibits an osmotic pressure of 3.0 atm at 300 K. Assuming the gas constant R = 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, the degree of dissociation of AB is approximately:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Calculate van't Hoff factor i = Π/CRT. CRT = 0.1 × 0.0821 × 300 ≈ 2.463. i = 3.0/2.463 ≈ 1.22. For AB ⇌ A⁺ + B⁻ (n=2), α = (i−1)/(n−1) = 0.22. Worked: Osmotic pressure Π = iCRT ⇒ i = Π/CRT = 3.0 / (0.1 × 0.0821 × 300) = 1.218. Degree of dissociation α = (i−1)/(ν−1) where ν=2 (ions produced). α = 0.218 ≈ 0.22.

questions.text: The rate constant of a reaction increases by a factor of 4 when the temperature is raised from 300 K to 310 K. The activation energy (Eₐ) of the reaction in kJ mol⁻¹ is closest to: (Use R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, ln 2 = 0.693)
questions.solution: Shortcut: Near 300 K, a 10 K rise doubles the rate for Eₐ ≈ 53.6 kJ mol⁻¹ (using ln2 = Eₐ/R × 10/300²). Since rate increases 4-fold (doubles twice), Eₐ ≈ 2 × 53.6 = 107.2 kJ mol⁻¹. Worked: Arrhenius equation: ln(k₂/k₁) = (Eₐ/R)(1/T₁ − 1/T₂). ln 4 = 2 ln 2 = 1.386. (1/300 − 1/310) = 10/93000 = 1/9300. Eₐ = 1.386 × 8.314 × 9300 ≈ 107,200 J mol⁻¹ = 107.2 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.text: Let ω be a complex cube root of unity (ω ≠ 1). The value of (1 - ω + ω^2)(1 + ω - ω^2) is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use 1+ω+ω^2=0 ⇒ 1+ω^2 = -ω and 1+ω = -ω^2. Then first factor = -2ω, second = -2ω^2. Product = 4ω^3 = 4. Full: Since ω^3=1 and 1+ω+ω^2=0, we have 1-ω+ω^2 = -2ω and 1+ω-ω^2 = -2ω^2. Multiplying gives 4ω^3 = 4.

questions.text: If A is a 3×3 matrix with determinant 2, then the determinant of adj(A) is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For any n×n matrix, |adj A| = |A|^{n-1}. Here n=3, so |adj A| = 2^{2} = 4. Full: The adjoint satisfies A·adj(A) = |A|I. Taking determinants gives |A|·|adj A| = |A|^3 ⇒ |adj A| = |A|^2 = 4.

questions.text: The value of the definite integral ∫_{-π/2}^{π/2} sin^3 x cos^2 x dx is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: The integrand f(x)=sin^3 x cos^2 x is an odd function because sin^3 x is odd and cos^2 x is even. Integral of an odd function over symmetric interval [-a,a] is zero. Full: Since f(-x) = -f(x), ∫_{-a}^{a} f(x) dx = 0. Here a=π/2, so the integral equals 0.

questions.text: The line y = 2x + c is a tangent to the ellipse x^2/9 + y^2/4 = 1. The value of c^2 is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1, the line y = mx + c is tangent iff c^2 = a^2 m^2 + b^2. Here a^2=9, b^2=4, m=2 ⇒ c^2 = 9·4 + 4 = 40. Full: Substitute y=2x+c into ellipse equation, set discriminant of resulting quadratic in x to zero. This yields c^2 = a^2 m^2 + b^2 = 40.

questions.text: Let S_nde note the sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic progression. If S_n = 3n^2 + 5n, then the common difference of the Apis:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For an AP, S_n = (d/2)n^2 + (a - d/2)n; comparing with 3n^2+5n gives d/2=3 ⇒ d=6. Full: a_n = S_n - S_{n-1} = 6n+2, so common difference d = a_n - a_{n-1} = 6.

questions.text: A solid sphere, a solid cylinder, and a thin ring, each of mass M and radius R, are released from rest at the top of a rough inclined plane of inclination θ. They roll without slipping. Which object reaches the bottom first?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Acceleration down an incline for rolling is a = g sinθ / (1 + k²/R²), where k is radius of gyration. The object with smallest k²/R² (sphere: 0.4) has maximum acceleration. Full: For rolling without slipping, mg sinθ - f = ma and fR = Iα = I(a/R). Solving gives a = g sinθ / (1 + I/mR²). Moments of inertia: Sphere = 2/5 mR², Cylinder = 1/2 mR², Ring = mR². Denominators are 1.4, 1.5, 2.0 respectively. Sphere has highest acceleration and reaches first.

questions.text: A satellite is orbiting very close to the Earth's surface (height h << R). What is the ratio of the escape velocity (v_e) from the Earth's surface to the orbital velocity (v_o) of this satellite?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Escape velocity v_e = √(2GM/R) = √(2gR). Orbital velocity near surface v_o = √(GM/R) = √(gR). Ratio v_e/v_o = √2. Full: Escape velocity is derived from energy conservation: 1/2 mv_e² = GMm/R. Orbital velocity from centripetal force: mv_o²/R = GMm/R². Dividing the two equations gives v_e²/v_o² = 2, so v_e/v_o = √2.

questions.text: For a diatomic ideal gas (γ = 7/5), what is the ratio of adiabatic bulk modulus to isothermal bulk modulus?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Isothermal bulk modulus B_iso = P. Adiabatic bulk modulus B_ad = γP. Ratio = γ = Cp/Cv = 7/5 = 1.4. Full: Bulk modulus B = -V(dP/dV). For isothermal process PV=constant => dP/P = -dV/V => B_iso = P. For adiabatic process PV^γ=constant => dP/P = -γ dV/V => B_ad = γP. Ratio B_ad/B_iso = γ = 1.4.

questions.text: The Boolean expression for the output Y of a logic circuit is Y = A·B + A'·B' (where ' denotes NOT). Which logic gate does this circuit represent?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The expression Y = AB + A'B' is the standard SOP form of an XNOR (Equivalence) gate. Output is HIGH (1) only when inputs are equal (A=B). Full: Truth table: A=0,B=0 => Y=1; A=0,B=1 => Y=0; A=1,B=0 => Y=0; A=1,B=1 => Y=1. This matches the XNOR gate truth table (output 1 for even number of 1s / equality).

questions.text: A series LCR circuit resonates at angular frequency ω₀. If the inductance is doubled (2L) and the capacitance is halved (C/2), what is the new resonant angular frequency?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Resonant frequency ω₀ = 1/√(LC). New product L'C' = (2L)×(C/2) = LC. Since LC product is unchanged, ω₀ remains same. Full: Original ω₀ = 1/√(LC). New ω₀' = 1/√(L'C') = 1/√((2L)(C/2)) = 1/√(LC) = ω₀.

questions.text: The half-life of a first order reaction is 20 minutes. The time required for 99% completion of the reaction is approximately:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For a first order reaction, t_99% ≈ 6.64 × t_1/2 (since ln(100)/ln(2) ≈ 4.605/0.693 = 6.64). 20 min × 6.64 ≈ 133 min. Full solution: k = ln2 / t_1/2 = 0.693/20 min⁻¹. For 99% completion, fraction remaining = 0.01, so t = (1/k) ln(1/0.01) = (20/0.693) × 4.605 ≈ 132.8 min ≈ 133 min.

questions.text: The EMF of the concentration cell Cu(s) | Cu²⁺(0.1 M) || Cu²⁺(0.01 M) | Cu(s) at 298 K is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For a concentration cell with n=2, E = (0.059/2) log₁₀(C₁/C₂). Here C₁/C₂ = 10, log10 = 1, so E = 0.0295 V. Full solution: Using Nernst equation, E = (RT/nF) ln(C₁/C₂) = (0.0591/2) log₁₀(0.1/0.01) = 0.02955 × 1 = 0.0295 V.

questions.text: Which of the following transition metal ions is colorless in aqueous solution due to the absence of d-d transitions?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Ions with d⁰ or d¹⁰ configuration have no d-d transitions and are colorless. Ti⁴⁺ is d⁰ (3d⁰), while V³⁺ (d²), Fe³⁺ (d⁵), Cu²⁺ (d⁹) have partially filled d-orbitals and are colored. Full solution: Electronic configuration of Ti⁴⁺ is [Ar] 3d⁰, so no d-d transition possible; hence it is colorless.

questions.text: For the gaseous reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), the value of Kp is 4.0 × 10⁻⁴ atm⁻² at 500 K. The value of Kc (in mol² L⁻²) at the same temperature is closest to: (R = 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
questions.solution: Shortcut: Δn_g = moles of gaseous products – moles of gaseous reactants = 2 – 4 = –2. Since Δn is negative, Kc = Kp(RT)². Calculate RT = 0.0821 × 500 ≈ 41. (RT)² ≈ 1681. Kc ≈ 4×10⁻⁴ × 1681 ≈ 0.67. Full Solution: The relationship is Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn. Here Δn = 2 – (1+3) = –2. Rearranging, Kc = Kp(RT)² = (4.0×10⁻⁴) × (0.0821 × 500)² = 4.0×10⁻⁴ × (41.05)² ≈ 4.0×10⁻⁴ × 1685 ≈ 0.674 mol² L⁻².

questions.text: Which of the following sets of monomers is used in the synthesis of Nylon-6,6?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The nomenclature 'Nylon-6,6' indicates a polyamide formed from two different monomers each containing 6 carbon atoms: a diamine (hexamethylenediamine, 6C) and a diacid (adipic acid, 6C). Nylon-6 uses caprolactam; Bakelite uses phenol/formaldehyde; Terylene (Dacron) uses ethylene glycol/terephthalic acid. Full Solution: Nylon-6,6 is a condensation polymer (polyamide) synthesized by the step-growth polymerization of hexamethylenediamine (H₂N–(CH₂)₆–NH₂) and adipic acid (HOOC–(CH₂)₄–COOH) with the elimination of water. The numbers 6,6 denote the number of carbon atoms in the diamine and the diacid respectively.

questions.text: The locus of the point of intersection of perpendicular tangents to the parabola y² = 8x is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For the parabola y² = 4ax, the locus of intersection of perpendicular tangents (Director Circle) is the directrix x = -a. Here 4a = 8 ⇒ a = 2, so the locus is x = -2. Full Solution: Equation of tangent to y² = 8x is y = mx + 2/m. If tangents from P(h, k) are perpendicular, m₁m₂ = -1. The combined equation of pair of tangents from (h, k) gives the condition h = -2. Thus the locus is x = -2.

questions.text: If A is a non-singular square matrix of order 3 such that |A| = 5, then the value of |adj(adj A)| is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For a non-singular matrix A of order n, |adj(adj A)| = |A|^((n-1)^2). Here n=3, |A|=5, so value = 5^4 = 625. Full: We know adj(adj A) = |A|^(n-2) * A. Taking determinant, |adj(adj A)| = | |A|^(n-2) A | = |A|^((n-2)n) * |A| = |A|^(n^2 - 2n + 1) = |A|^((n-1)^2). Substituting n=3, |A|=5 gives 5^4 = 625.

questions.text: For a binomial distribution B(n, p), the mean is 4 and the variance is 3. The probability of at least one success is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For Binomial, q = Variance/Mean = 3/4, so p = 1/4. Then n = Mean/p = 4/(1/4) = 16. P(at least 1 success) = 1 - P(0 success) = 1 - qⁿ = 1 - (3/4)¹⁶. Full: Given np = 4 and npq = 3. Dividing, q = 3/4 ⇒ p = 1/4. Substituting in np=4 gives n(1/4)=4 ⇒ n=16. P(X ≥ 1) = 1 - P(X=0) = 1 - ⁿC₀ p⁰ qⁿ = 1 - (3/4)¹⁶.

questions.text: The equation of the polar of the point (2, 3) with respect to the circle x² + y² = 9 is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: The polar of (x₁, y₁) w.r.t. circle x²+y²=a² is T=0 i.e., xx₁+yy₁=a². For (2,3) and a²=9: 2x+3y=9. Full: The given circle is x²+y²=9. The equation of the polar (chord of contact) of an external point (x₁, y₁) is obtained by replacing x²→xx₁, y²→yy₁ in the circle equation (T=0 form). Thus, x(2) + y(3) = 9 ⇒ 2x + 3y = 9.

questions.text: The coefficient of x^5 in the expansion of (1+x)^10 (1-x)^10 is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: (1+x)^10(1-x)^10 = (1-x^2)^10, which contains only even powers of x, so the coefficient of x^5 is 0. Full solution: The product simplifies to (1-x^2)^10 = Σ_{k=0}^{10} C(10,k)(-1)^k x^{2k}. Since 5 is odd, no term with x^5 exists, giving coefficient 0.

questions.text: In a photoelectric experiment, light of frequency 1.5 times the threshold frequency is incident on a metal surface. If the work function of the metal is φ, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Using Einstein's photoelectric equation K_max = hν - φ. Since ν = 1.5 ν₀ and φ = hν₀, K_max = 1.5φ - φ = 0.5φ. Full solution: The threshold frequency ν₀ satisfies φ = hν₀. Incident frequency ν = 1.5ν₀ gives photon energy hν = 1.5hν₀ = 1.5φ. Subtracting work function yields K_max = 1.5φ - φ = 0.5φ.

questions.text: A horizontal platform of moment of inertia 0.5 kg·m² rotates freely at 2 rad/s. A person standing at the centre holds two weights (1 kg each) at arm's length 1 m from the axis. He suddenly pulls the weights inward to 0.5 m. The new angular speed of the platform (in rad/s) is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Angular momentum L = Iω is conserved (no external torque). Initial I = I_platform + 2mr₁² = 0.5 + 2(1)(1)² = 2.5 kg·m². Final I = 0.5 + 2(1)(0.5)² = 1.0 kg·m². Since I decreases by factor 2.5, ω increases by factor 2.5: ω_f = 2 × 2.5 = 5 rad/s. Detailed: L_i = L_f ⇒ (I_p + 2mr₁²)ω_i = (I_p + 2mr₂²)ω_f ⇒ ω_f = ω_i × (0.5 + 2) / (0.5 + 0.5) = 2 × 2.5 = 5 rad/s.

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance C₀ is charged to Q₀ and disconnected from the battery. A dielectric slab of constant K = 2 and thickness equal to half the plate separation is inserted between the plates. The new energy stored in the capacitor is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Battery disconnected ⇒ Q constant. Energy U = Q²/(2C). Slab creates two capacitors in series: air gap (d/2) ⇒ C₁ = 2C₀; dielectric (d/2, K=2) ⇒ C₂ = 4C₀. Equivalent C = (C₁C₂)/(C₁+C₂) = 8C₀²/6C₀ = 4C₀/3. U_f = Q₀²/(2 × 4C₀/3) = 3Q₀²/(8C₀). Detailed: Initial energy U_i = Q₀²/(2C₀). Final capacitance C_f = ε₀A / (d/2 + (d/2)/K) = ε₀A / (d/2 + d/4) = (4/3)ε₀A/d = 4C₀/3. U_f = Q₀²/(2C_f) = 3Q₀²/(8C₀).

questions.text: One mole of a diatomic ideal gas (γ = 7/5) undergoes an adiabatic expansion such that its volume becomes twice the initial volume. The ratio of final temperature to initial temperature (T₂/T₁) is:

questions.text: A conducting rod of length L rotates with constant angular velocity ω about one end in a uniform magnetic field B directed perpendicular to the plane of rotation. The induced emf between the two ends of the rod is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: The rod sweeps a circular area; rate of area swept = ½L²ω. By Faraday's law, emf = B × dA/dt = ½BωL². Full derivation: Consider an element dr at distance r. Its velocity v = ωr. Motional emf in element = Bv dr = Bωr dr. Integrating from 0 to L gives υ = Bω −⁻⁰ r dr = ½BωL².

questions.text: The value of the definite integral ∫₀^{π/2} (sin³x)/(sin³x + cos³x) dx is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use King's Property: I = ∫₀^{π/2} f(sin x, cos x) dx = ∫₀^{π/2} f(cos x, sin x) dx. Let I be the given integral. Replacing x by π/2 - x gives I = ∫₀^{π/2} (cos³x)/(cos³x + sin³x) dx. Adding the two expressions: 2I = ∫₀^{π/2} 1 dx = π/2 ⇒ I = π/4. Full Solution: Let I = ∫₀^{π/2} sin³x/(sin³x+cos³x) dx. Substitute x → π/2 - x: I = ∫₀^{π/2} cos³x/(sin³x+cos³x) dx. Adding: 2I = ∫₀^{π/2} (sin³x+cos³x)/(sin³x+cos³x) dx = ∫₀^{π/2} dx = π/2. Therefore, I = π/4.

questions.text: There are 10 points in a plane, no three of which are collinear except 4 points which are collinear. The number of triangles that can be formed by joining these points is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Total triangles from 10 points = ¹⁰C₃ = 120. Triangles lost due to 4 collinear points = ⁴C₃ = 4. Required triangles = 120 - 4 = 116. Full Solution: Select any 3 points out of 10 to form a triangle in ¹⁰C₃ ways. However, any 3 points chosen from the 4 collinear points do not form a triangle. Subtract these ⁴C₃ invalid cases. ¹⁰C₃ - ⁴C₃ = 120 - 4 = 116.
questions.topic: Permutations and Combinations (Combinations with Collinear Points)

questions.text: If ω is a non-real cube root of unity, then the value of (1 - ω + ω²)⁴ + (1 + ω - ω²)⁴ is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use 1+ω+ω²=0 ⇒ 1+ω²=-ω and 1+ω=-ω². Then (1-ω+ω²)=-2ω and (1+ω-ω²)=-2ω². The expression becomes 16ω⁴+16ω⁸=16(ω+ω²)=16(-1)=-16. Full Solution: Since ω³=1 and 1+ω+ω²=0, we have 1+ω²=-ω and 1+ω=-ω². First bracket: (1+ω²)-ω = -ω-ω = -2ω. Second bracket: (1+ω)-ω² = -ω²-ω² = -2ω². Raising to power 4: (-2ω)⁴ + (-2ω²)⁴ = 16ω⁴ + 16ω⁸ = 16ω + 16ω² = 16(ω+ω²) = -16.

questions.text: If A is a square matrix of order 3 such that |A| = 3, then |adj(adj A)| is equal to:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For a square matrix of order n, |adj A| = |A|^{n-1}. Applying twice: |adj(adj A)| = |A|^{(n-1)²}. For n=3, |adj(adj A)| = |A|⁴ = 3⁴ = 81. Full Solution: We know A(adj A) = |A|I. Taking determinants: |A| |adj A| = |A|³ ⇒ |adj A| = |A|² = 9. Now treat adj A as a new matrix B of order 3 with |B| = 9. Then |adj B| = |B|² = 9² = 81. Thus |adj(adj A)| = 81.

questions.text: Number of solutions of the equation sin 2x = cos x in the interval [0, 2π] is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use identity sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x to factorize as cos x (2 sin x - 1) = 0. Solve cos x = 0 (gives π/2, 3π/2) and sin x = 1/2 (gives π/6, 5π/6) separately in [0, 2π]. Total 4 distinct solutions. Full Solution: sin 2x = cos x ⇒ 2 sin x cos x - cos x = 0 ⇒ cos x (2 sin x - 1) = 0. Case 1: cos x = 0 ⇒ x = π/2, 3π/2. Case 2: sin x = 1/2 ⇒ x = π/6, 5π/6. All four values are distinct and lie in [0, 2π]. Hence, 4 solutions.
